```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(mgcv) # gam
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(splines) #bsplines
library(rjags)
library(purrr)
```



NOTE: the data code is inwithout_zoo_longer_period.Rmd + data_handling.Rmd


```{r}
#Step 1
#complete cases

complete_vars <- complete.cases(
  eymir_seasonal_df_long[, c("log_din", "din_lag7", "mean_depth","mean_temp", "Month", "fish_removal", "log_srp",
                            "srp_lag7", "large_biomass","small_biomass","mean_secchi", "log_din_lag1", "log_din_lag7","log_srp_lag7","log_chla_lag7")] 
  ) # other variable will be added as the model proceeds

df_long_period_clean <- eymir_seasonal_df_long[complete_vars,]

### Check this step
cat("Rows after complete case filter:", nrow(df_long_period_clean), "\n")


```
  

```{r}
#Step 2
# Fitting the GAM for din
##### gam model bayes starter

din_gam_ps_f <- gam(log_din ~ mean_depth + mean_temp   + s(IntLoadDIN, bs="ps", k= 10),   data = eymir_seasonal_df_long, method= "REML") 
#  what about by=month but lag1, and #lag7 yapınca depth significant but, r^2 low

din_gam_f <- gam(log_din ~ mean_depth + mean_temp   + IntLoadDIN,   data = eymir_seasonal_df_long, method= "REML") 
#  what about by=month but lag1, and #lag7 yapınca depth significant but, r^2 low

summary(din_gam_ps_f)
summary(din_gam_f)
```


```{r}
#Step3
#### Extracting knots from the GAM 
## as the model proceeds other parameter chuncks can be added 

smooth_din <- din_gam_ps_f$smooth[[1]] # first smooth term (din_lag7)

knots_used_din <- smooth_din$knots # knots sequence mgcv used

order_din <- smooth_din$m[1]+2  #spline order (4= cubic)

cat("din_lag7: knots=", length(knots_used_din),
    "| spline order =", order_din, "\n")



```


```{r}
#Step4
## call x from df_long_period_clean, so that rows align with y, depth, temp, etc


b_din <- splineDesign(
  knots = knots_used_din,
  x= df_long_period_clean$IntLoadDIN, # from the cleaned data frame
  ord = order_din, 
  outer.ok = TRUE
)
## NOTE: write more explanations

b_din_centered <- scale(b_din, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)


K_din <- ncol(b_din) # number of basis functions for din smooth

cat("b_din dimensions:", nrow(b_din), "x", K_din, "\n")

```


```{r}
#Step 5

N <- nrow(df_long_period_clean) #number of shared row number

#n_months <- length(unique(df_long_period_clean$Month))

#covariates

depth_s <- as.numeric(scale(df_long_period_clean$mean_depth))
temp_s <- as.numeric(scale(df_long_period_clean$mean_temp))


# sanity check - eveything must have length N ##### this part is recommended by AI

stopifnot(nrow(b_din) == N)
stopifnot(length(df_long_period_clean$log_din_lag7) == N)
stopifnot(length(depth_s) == N)
stopifnot(length(temp_s)  == N)
cat("All dimensions check passed. N =", N, "\n")

```


```{r}
# Step 6 


jags_data_din <- list(
  N              = N,
  K_din          = K_din,
  y_din          = df_long_period_clean$log_din,
  b_din_centered = b_din_centered,
  depth          = depth_s,
  temp           = temp_s      # ← no comma here
)

# Final check — print length/nrow of every element # AI recommended
cat("jags_data dimensions:\n")
sapply(jags_data_din, function(x) if (is.matrix(x)) nrow(x) else length(x))

 din_basis_center <- attr(b_din_centered, "scaled:center")

```

```{r}
#Step 7

model_string_din <- "
model{

#Likelihood

for( i in 1:N){
y_din[i] ~ dnorm(mu_din[i], tau_y_din) # likelihood function

mu_din[i] <- alpha_din + #intercept
             beta_depth * depth[i] + # covariates 
             beta_temp * temp[i] +
             inprod(b_din_centered[i,], coef_din[1:K_din])
             
           
             
}

#P-spline prior : log_din_lag7 
# second_order random-walk -penalises curvature
# add the folloeing  block for smooths

coef_din[1] ~dnorm(0, 0.0001) 
# flat prior : different treatment due to not having j-1 and j-2
coef_din[2]~dnorm(0, 0.0001) 
# flat priors because we cannot penalise them
 
 for (j in 3:K_din){
 coef_din[j] ~ dnorm(2*coef_din[j-1]- coef_din[j-2], tau_b_din)
 #curvature penalty means that each new coef should not deviate much from the linear trend of the previous two
 }

## parametric priors

alpha_din ~dnorm(0, 0.0001) # intercept for din
beta_depth ~dnorm(0, 0.0001) # effect of mean_depth
beta_temp ~ dnorm(0, 0.0001) # effect of mean_temp

#for (m in 1 :n_months){
#beta_month[m] ~ dnorm(0, 0.0001) # month_specific intercept shifts

 
#hyperpriors 

tau_y_din    ~ dgamma(2, 0.5)          # weakly informative residual precision
sigma_b_din  ~ dexp(7.3)                 # smoothing SD — same fix as SRP depth
tau_b_din    <- 1 / (sigma_b_din * sigma_b_din)


#derived quantities

sigma_y_din <- 1/ sqrt(tau_y_din) # residual for SD for din

 }

"
```


```{r}
#Step 8

inits_din <- function() list(
  alpha_din = 0,
  beta_depth = 0,
  beta_temp = 0,
  coef_din = rep(0, K_din),
  tau_y_din = 1,
  sigma_b_din = 1
  #coef_srp = rep(0,K_srp),
)

library(rjags) ######


jags_model_din <- jags.model(
  textConnection(model_string_din),
  data = jags_data_din,
  inits= inits_din,
  n.chains = 3,
  n.adapt = 1000
)

#Burn-in
update(jags_model_din, n.iter= 2000)

#sample

params_to_monitor <- c(
  "alpha_din", "beta_depth", "beta_temp","coef_din", "sigma_y_din","sigma_b_din"
  # add "coef_srp", "sigma_y_srp"
)

samples_din <- coda.samples(
  jags_model_din,
  variable.names = params_to_monitor,
  n.iter = 10000,
  thin = 2
)

summary(samples_din)


##### corrections needed in this code especialaly at depth, temp etc part
```

note on thinning: 
Therefore, it is standard to make inference on "thinned" chains where only a fraction of the MCMC iterations are used in inference (e.g. only every fifth, tenth, or hundredth iteration, depending on the severity of the autocorrelation).

on adaptation phase:
When a JAGS model is compiled, it may require an initial sampling phase during which the samplers adapt their behaviour to maximize their efficiency (e.g. a Metropolis-Hastings random walk algorithm may change its step size). The sequence of samples generated during this adaptive phase is not a Markov chain, and therefore may not be used for posterior inference on the model.
```{r}
# ── Clean reset may be needed

# ── Fresh chain function ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fresh_chains_din <- function(n_iter) {
  
  jags_model_diag_din <- jags.model(
    textConnection(model_string_din),
    data     = jags_data_din,
    inits    = inits_list_din,
    n.chains = 3,
    n.adapt  = 1          # no adaptation
  )
  
  samples_din <- coda.samples(
    jags_model_diag_din,
    variable.names = c("alpha_din", "beta_depth", "beta_temp",
                        "sigma_y_din", "sigma_b_din"),
    n.iter = n_iter,      # uses the argument, not hardcoded 5000
    thin   = 1
  )
  
  return(samples_din)
}

# ── Run ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
samples_diag_din <- fresh_chains_din(n_iter = 12000)

# ── Verify ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cat("Iterations per chain:", nrow(samples_diag_din[[1]]), "\n")  # must be 5000

# ── Convert to long df ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
params_diag_din <- c("alpha_din", "beta_depth", "beta_temp",
                      "sigma_y_din", "sigma_b_din")

chains_df_din <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(c) {
  df <- as.data.frame(samples_diag_din[[c]])
  df$iteration <- 1:nrow(df)
  df$chain     <- paste0("Chain ", c)
  df
})) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols      = all_of(params_diag_din),
               names_to  = "parameter",
               values_to = "value")

# ── One plot per parameter ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
params_diag_din %>% walk(function(param) {
  
  p <- chains_df_din %>%
    filter(parameter == param) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = iteration, y = value, colour = chain)) +
    geom_line(alpha = 0.8, linewidth = 0.4) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("Chain 1" = "#E05C2A",
                                   "Chain 2" = "#2A6EA0",
                                   "Chain 3" = "#4DAF4A")) +
    labs(
      title    = paste0("Trace: ", param),
      subtitle = "3 chains from different starting values | no adaptation | no burn-in",
      x        = "Iteration",
      y        = "Value",
      colour   = NULL
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      legend.position  = "top",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
  
  print(p)
})

```



```{r}
# Or with ggplot via tidybayes for cleaner output
library(bayesplot)
mcmc_trace(samples_diag_din,
           pars = c("alpha_din", "beta_depth", "beta_temp",
                    "sigma_y_din", "sigma_b_din"))

# ── Gelman-Rubin diagnostic — values close to 1.00 = converged ───────────────
gelman.diag(samples_diag_din)
gelman.plot(samples_diag_din)   # shows convergence over iterations
```
